'''George Alvin Wiley''' (February 26, 1931 – August 8, 1973) was an American [[chemist]] and [[civil rights]] leader. He was a founder of the [[National Welfare Rights Organization]].

==Early life and education==
Wiley was born in [[Bayonne, New Jersey]], the son of a postal clerk and one of six children. Wiley's family eventually moved to [[Warwick, Rhode Island]].

Wiley earned his undergraduate degree at the [[University of Rhode Island]] in 1953. Working with [[Jerrold Meinwald]], he received a doctorate in organic chemistry from [[Cornell University]] in 1957.<ref>{{cite thesis |type=PhD |last1=Wiley |first1=George Alvin |title=I: The structure of flavothebaone II. The synthesis of some benzo- (1', 2', 5, 6)- norbornenes. |oclc=745509949 |url=https://www.proquest.com/openview/286dda62f4a32318cabd80591197efc5/1?pq-origsite=gscholar&cbl=18750 |access-date=23 December 2021 |publisher=[[Cornell University]] |date=June 1957 |language=en}}</ref> Wiley fulfilled a six-month [[ROTC]] obligation as a first lieutenant in the [[United States Army]] at [[Fort Lee, Virginia]]; and subsequently accepted  a post-doctoral fellowship at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]].

==Career==
Wiley taught for two years at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], whereupon he took a teaching position at [[Syracuse University]] in 1960. In November 1961, he founded the Syracuse chapter of [[Congress of Racial Equality]]. He was only the third Black faculty member at Syracuse.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Searing |first1=Robert |title=SU professor George Wiley led the struggle to end segregation in Syracuse |url=https://www.syracuse.com/living/2022/02/su-professor-george-wiley-led-the-struggle-to-end-segregation-in-syracuse.html |access-date=4 February 2022 |work=[[The Post-Standard]] |date=3 February 2022 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Hippensteel |first1=Chris |title=SU Students vs. 'The Deep North': Syracuse's Urban Renewal Protests, 60 years later |url=https://dailyorange.com/2023/10/urban-renewal-protests-1963-60-years-later-syracuse-university-congress-of-racial-equality/ |access-date=30 October 2023 |work=[[The Daily Orange]] |date=30 October 2023}}</ref> He later was a founder of the [[National Welfare Rights Organization]].<ref name="nyt">{{Cite news|date=1973-08-10|title=DR. GEORGE WILEY FEARED DROWNED|language=en-US|work=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1973/08/10/archives/dr-george-wiley-feared-drowned-civil-rights-leader-42-who-headed.html|access-date=2022-02-04|issn=0362-4331}}</ref>

He was listed on the [[Master list of Nixon's political opponents]].{{cn|date=December 2021}}

The ''George Wiley Award for Exceptional Performance in Organic Chemistry'' for students at Syracuse University is named in his honor.<ref>{{cite news |title=Chemistry Department honors students with annual awards |url=https://news.syr.edu/blog/2011/05/02/chemistry-department-honors-students-with-annual-awards/ |access-date=23 December 2021 |work=Syracuse University News |date=2 May 2011}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Wiley married and had two children. His daughter is civil rights activist and lawyer, [[Maya Wiley]].<ref name="politico">{{cite web |website=[[Politico]] |url=https://www.politico.com/story/2014/07/maya-wiley-new-york-city-mayor-counsel-109162 |title=Maya Wiley's push for civil rights |date=July 21, 2014 }}</ref>

==Death==
On August 8, 1973, Wiley fell overboard while on a boat with his children on the [[Chesapeake Bay]].<ref name="nyt"/><ref>{{Cite news|date=1973-08-10|title=Dr. George Wiley Feared Drowned|language=en-US|work=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1973/08/10/archives/dr-george-wiley-feared-drowned-civil-rights-leader-42-who-headed.html|access-date=2020-05-31|issn=0362-4331}}</ref> On August 12, 1973, Wiley's body was found on the shore of [[Chesapeake Beach, Maryland]] after a three-day search.<ref>{{Cite news|date=1973-08-12|title=Body of Dr. George Wiley Recovered and Identified|language=en-US|work=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1973/08/12/archives/body-of-dr-george-wiley-recovered-and-identified.html|access-date=2020-05-31|issn=0362-4331}}</ref>
